'''Arinze Christopher Onuaku''' ({{Audio |LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Ebube Clara-Arinze Christopher Onuaku.wav |listern|help=no}}; born July 13, 1987) is an American [[basketball]] coach and former player who is currently an assistant coach for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC), his alma mater.

==High school career==
Onuaku attended [[DuVal High School]] in Lanham, Maryland before transferring in 2003, following his sophomore year, to [[Episcopal High School (Alexandria, Virginia)|Episcopal High School]] in [[Alexandria, Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ethan|last=Ramsey|url=http://www.dailyorange.com/2005/04/mbb-arinze-onuaku-the-next-big-thing/|title=MBB: Arinze Onuaku: The next big thing|work=DailyOrange.com|date=April 16, 2005|access-date=July 8, 2014}}</ref> As a senior in 2004–05, he earned the Episcopal High School William Caskie Watts MVP Award after helping his squad to a 12–11 record.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://cuse.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6925|title=Arinze Onuaku - 2009-10 Men's Basketball|work=Cuse.com|access-date=July 8, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], Onuaku was named to the Big East Conference All-Academic Team and earned SU Athletic Director's Honor Roll recognition in each of his first two semesters. In 29 games, he averaged 2.0 points and 2.8 rebounds per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/arinze-onuaku-1.html|title=Arinze Onuaku Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=July 8, 2014}}</ref>

In October 2006, Onuaku underwent surgery on his left knee and subsequently redshirted the 2006–07 season. He was, however, named to the Big East Conference All-Academic Team and earned SU Athletic Director's Honor Roll recognition for the second straight year following the fall and spring semesters.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his redshirted sophomore season, Onuaku ranked second in the Big East Conference and ninth in the nation in field-goal percentage with 62.8%. He was named to the Big East Conference All-Academic Team for the third straight year, and was on the SU Athletic Director's Honor Roll for the fall semester. In 35 games, he averaged 12.7 points, 8.1 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 1.3 blocks per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, Onuaku was again named to the SU Athletic Director's Honor Roll for the fall semester. In 38 games, he averaged 10.3 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, Onuaku became the 52nd player in Syracuse history to score 1,000 points with four against Florida on December 10, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Waters|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2009/12/sweat_equity_arinze_onuakus_pa.html|title=Sweat Equity: Arinze Onuaku's path to 1,000 points|work=Syracuse.com|date=December 16, 2009|access-date=July 8, 2014}}</ref> For the fourth straight year, he was named to the SU Athletic Director's Honor Roll for the fall semester. He also earned 2009 Pre-season All-Big East Honorable Mention honors. In March 2010, he suffered a season-ending leg injury during the Big East Tournament quarter-finals against Georgetown. In 32 games (31 starts), he averaged 10.5 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.1 blocks in 22.8 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

Onuaku finished his career first on the Syracuse all-time list with a .648 field goal percentage (540-for-833), and 11th all-time with 148 blocked shots.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===2010–11 season===
Onuaku went undrafted in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On March 2, 2011, he was acquired by the Rio Grande Valley Vipers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/onuaku030211.html |title=Vipers Acquire Former Syracuse Star |work=NBA.com |date=March 2, 2011 |access-date=July 8, 2014 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714203500/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/onuaku030211.html |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

===2011–12 season===
On September 14, 2011, Onuaku signed with [[BC Neptūnas|Klaipėdos Neptūnas]] of Lithuania for the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/lithuania/88390/neptunas-lands-arinze-onuaku.html|title=Neptunas lands Arinze Onuaku|work=Sportando.com|date=September 14, 2011|access-date=July 8, 2014}}</ref> In December 2011, he parted ways with Neptūnas following a knee injury.

===2012–13 season===
On November 2, 2012, Onuaku was selected by the Reno Bighorns in the fourth round of the 2012 NBA Development League draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/bighorns-select-eight-players-in-nba-d-league-draft/n-4506981|title=Bighorns Select Eight Players in NBA D-League Draft|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 2, 2012|access-date=January 6, 2017}}</ref> Three days later, he was traded to the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/charge-make-roster-moves/n-4508246|title=Charge Make Roster Moves|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 5, 2012|access-date=January 6, 2017}}</ref> On February 4, 2013, he was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced |work=NBA.com |date=February 4, 2013 |access-date=February 4, 2013 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812091051/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |archive-date=August 12, 2016 }}</ref>

===2013–14 season===
In July 2013, Onuaku joined the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-announce-2013-nba-summer-league-roster|title=Suns Announce 2013 NBA Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2013|access-date=July 8, 2013}}</ref> and on August 22, 2013, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-lance-thomas-and-arinze-onuaku|title=PELICANS SIGN LANCE THOMAS AND ARINZE ONUAKU|work=NBA.com|date=August 22, 2013|access-date=August 22, 2013}}</ref> However, they waived him on November 12.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-amundson-and-childress|title=PELICANS SIGN AMUNDSON AND CHILDRESS|work=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2013|access-date=November 12, 2013}}</ref> On November 27, he was re-acquired by the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/chrge_sign_onuku___return_2013_11_27.html |title=Charge Acquire Onuaku as Returning Player |work=NBA.com |date=November 27, 2013 |access-date=November 27, 2013 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211143142/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/chrge_sign_onuku___return_2013_11_27.html |archive-date=December 11, 2013 }}</ref> On February 13, 2014, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2014 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]], as a replacement for [[Dewayne Dedmon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/replacements_for_all_star_2014_02_13.html |title=Replacements Announced For 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire |work=NBA.com |date=February 13, 2014 |access-date=February 13, 2014 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325092506/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/replacements_for_all_star_2014_02_13.html |archive-date=March 25, 2015 }}</ref>

On February 22, 2014, Onuaku signed a 10-day contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/onuaku-signing-140222|title=Cavs Sign Arinze Onuaku to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2014|access-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref> He was assigned back down to the Charge the same day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/assign-onuaku-140222|title=Cavs Assign Onuaku to Charge|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2014|access-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref> The next day, he was recalled by the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-onuaku-140223|title=Cavs Recall Onuaku from Charge|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2014|access-date=February 23, 2014}}</ref> On March 4, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavs-sign-onuaku-140304|title=Cavs Sign Arinze Onuaku to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2014|access-date=March 4, 2014}}</ref> On March 8, he was reassigned to the Charge. He was recalled the same day after playing in the Charge's 118–110 win over the [[Idaho Stampede]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/pair-of-cavs-assignments-lead-charge-to-win/n-4748900|title=Pair of Cavs Assignments Lead Charge to Win|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 8, 2014|access-date=March 8, 2014}}</ref> He also received assignments to the Charge on March 9 and March 11.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|archive-date=March 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 12, he was waived by the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/sign-edwards-10-day-140312|title=Cavs Sign Shane Edwards to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 12, 2014|access-date=March 12, 2014}}</ref> The next day, he was re-acquired by the Charge.

In May 2014, Onuaku joined the [[Chongqing Flying Dragons]] for the 2014 [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] season. He left the team in late June after averaging 28.6 points and 14.8 rebounds in 19 games.

===2014–15 season===
In July 2014, Onuaku joined the Indiana Pacers for the [[2014 NBA Summer League|Orlando Summer League]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/rookie/free-agent-camp-update|title=Rookie/Free Agent Camp Update|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2014|access-date=July 8, 2014}}</ref> and the New Orleans Pelicans for the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 5, he signed with the Pacers,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-four-players|title=Pacers Sign Four Free Agents|work=NBA.com|date=September 5, 2014|access-date=September 5, 2014}}</ref> only to be waived by the team on October 25.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-four-players|title=Pacers Waive Four Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2014|access-date=October 25, 2014}}</ref> On November 22, he was reacquired by the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/onuaku_returns__charge_2014_11_22.html |title=Arinze Onuaku Returns to Canton Charge |work=NBA.com |date=November 22, 2014 |access-date=November 22, 2014 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201114131/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/onuaku_returns__charge_2014_11_22.html |archive-date=February 1, 2015 }}</ref> On February 4, 2015, he was named to his third Futures All-Star team, this time for the 2015 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|title=Thirteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=February 15, 2015|access-date=February 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205023335/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|archive-date=February 5, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On April 7, 2015, Onuaku signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the rest of the season to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Minnesota had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-sign-forward-arinze-onuaku|title=Wolves Sign Forward Arinze Onuaku|work=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2015|access-date=April 7, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Timberwolves later that day, recording 6 points and 5 rebounds in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Wagaman|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150407/MINSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Kings hold off Timberwolves behind Casspi|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref>

===2015–16 season===
[[File:PBA - Meralco vs Alaska - Arinze Onuaku - Meralco - 2016-0425 (26374015110).jpg|thumb|right|150px|Onuaku during his stint with the [[Meralco Bolts]].]]
In July 2015, Onuaku joined the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the Orlando Summer League and the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. On October 6, 2015, he signed a three-month contract with Israeli powerhouse team [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/news/i/6e35d4dptm7ox3b8/maccabi-adds-size-with-onuaku|title=Maccabi adds size with Onuaku|work=Euroleague.net|date=October 6, 2015|access-date=October 6, 2015|archive-date=January 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129233104/http://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/news/i/6e35d4dptm7ox3b8/maccabi-adds-size-with-onuaku|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.walla.co.il/item/2894736|title=מכבי תל אביב: הסנטר הניגרי ארינזה אונואקו חתם רשמית|work=Walla.co.il|date=October 6, 2015|access-date=October 6, 2015|language=he}}</ref> On January 22, 2016, Onuaku was released by Maccabi, after he declined a one-month contract extension offered by the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport5.co.il/articles.aspx?FolderID=274&docID=204400|title=מקל יערוך בכורה מול נס ציונה. אונוואקו שוחרר|work=Sport5.co.il|date=January 22, 2016|access-date=January 22, 2016|language=he}}</ref>

On February 6, 2016, Onuaku signed with the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as the team's import for the [[2016 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Karlo|last=Sacamos|url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/arinze-onuaku-replaces-injured-malcolm-thomas-in-last-minute-import-change-for-meralco|title=Arinze Onuaku replaces injured Malcolm Thomas in last-minute import change for Bolts|work=Spin.ph|date=February 6, 2016|access-date=February 6, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Rey|last=Joble|url=http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/meralcos-import-replacement-arinze-onuaku-arrives-in-time-for-commissioners-cup-opener|title=Meralco's import replacement Arinze Onuaku arrives in time for Commissioner's Cup opener|work=InterAksyon.com|date=February 10, 2016|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> He went on to win the [[Bobby Parks PBA Best Import of the Conference award|PBA Best Import of the Conference Award]].

===2016–17 season===
In July 2016, Onuaku joined the [[Orlando Magic]] white team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League|2016 Orlando Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Carlson|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2016/07/arinze_onuaku_finishes_nba_summer_league_averaging_almost_a_double-double.html|title=Arinze Onuaku finishes NBA Summer League averaging almost a double-double|work=Syracuse.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> On September 8, 2016, he signed with the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-six-free-agents-training-camp-nick-johnson-cliff-alexander-damjan-rudez-20160908|title=Orlando Magic Sign Six Players|date=September 8, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> On January 6, 2017, he was waived by the Magic after appearing in eight games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-arinze-onuaku-recall-cj-wilcox|title=Magic Waive Arinze Onuaku; Recall C.J. Wilcox|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=January 6, 2017}}</ref>

On June 8, 2017, Onuaku signed with [[Hunan Yongsheng]] of China for the 2017 [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Arinze Onuaku to play with Hunan in China|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/236437/arinze-onuaku-to-play-with-hunan-in-china.html|access-date=June 10, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=June 8, 2017}}</ref>

===2017–18 season===
Onuaku signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] for the remainder of the 2017–18 season on February 5, 2018, after the team waived [[Jarnell Stokes]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180203101243/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-02/03/c_136946407.htm CBA side Zhejiang parts ways with former NBA player Stokes, accusing him of "being unprofessional].XINHUANET.com.[2018-02-03].</ref>

In March 2018, Onuaku signed again with the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as their import for the [[2018 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tv5.espn.com/basketball/pba/story/_/id/22648769/white-macklin-onuaku-return-pba-commissioner-cup|title=White, Macklin, Onuaku to return for PBA Commissioner's Cup|date=5 March 2018 }}</ref>

==The Basketball Tournament==
Arinze Onuaku played for Boeheim's Army in the 2018 edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. In 4 games, he averaged 9.5 points, 5.8 rebounds, and .5 blocks per game. Boeheim's Army reached the Northeast Regional Championship before falling to the Golden Eagles.

==Coaching career==
Onuaku was hired as an assistant coach at [[Siena Saints men's basketball|Siena College]] in 2024 after serving as an assistant coach in a variety of capacities since his playing career ended.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2024/05/former-syracuse-basketball-center-arinze-will-work-for-gerry-mcnamara-at-siena-its-a-big-move.html| title=Former Syracuse Basketball Center Arinze Will Work for Gerry McNamara at Siena. It's a Big Move| website=[[syracuse.com]]| first=Donna| last=Ditota| date=May 9, 2024| access-date=November 7, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Onuaku is the son of Christopher and Anastasia Onuaku,<ref name="bio" /> and has three siblings: Ify, [[Chinanu Onuaku|Chinanu]] and Michael.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://igbopeople.blogspot.com.au/2009/03/arinze-onuaku.html|title=Celebrating Ndi-Igbo: Arinze Onuaku|work=IgboPeople.blogspot.com.au|date=March 26, 2009|access-date=March 26, 2009}}</ref> Chinanu is also a professional basketball player.
